questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me to study in a country where I was able to speak German, which I have been practicing. Further, it was important that I was not stuyding in a too small city, and that the administrative hurdle of going on exchange was minimal.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up having a lot of problem with housing, which caused me a lot of stress and put financial strain on me. It was hard to find a place to live and the options were more expensive than advertised by the guest university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not very easy, but not very hard. I think it would have been much harder if I had not started with the other students at the language course as I would not have found organisations such as ESN Frankfurt.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a "buddy" from the guest university. However, it was first a couple of weeks after arrivial, which meant that he could not help me with the most cruicial parts of my settling in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The institute always replied fast and was helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard. I found a room through WG-Gesucht which was expensive. I ended up having to move after a month, because I had a bad relationship with my roomate. I fonud private student housing through a friend of mine in Frankfurt who lived in the same building.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Expect the price to be higher than 250-350 EUR per month. My rent was 960 EUR.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I gained limited help from the university and received information late about my lack of housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. My main problem was that, as I took courses from multiple study lines, to figure out which institute I should apply under.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was smooth and easy. I just had to understand the system at Goethe first.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was able to write to the international department and they answered fast and was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. I liked that I had a week or two to try out the classes before registering. However, the course catalogue changed a lot before arrival, meaning I got very different courses than the ones originally intended.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To not expect that the same courses being offered now will be offered the semester you go - be prepared for changes. Don't be afraid to text the university, they will help you find the right person to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level high. I did not find them particularly mathematically challenging compared to economics at KU. But I found them insightful in other ways.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
You have to write many more notes! Usually at KU we only nede to look at the slidedecks, and then write a few notes if the teacher says something extra. In Frankfurt, you need a whole separate note taking system. It took me a while to get used to. You can also not expect to have the solutions uploaded. 

Secondly, at economics at KU we have separate courses teaching methdology. At Frankfurt, methodology is intertwined with the courses, i.e. you learn econometric methods in "Development Economics II", where we have a separate econometric course for the methods in KU.

Otherwise it was similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* The Winners and Losers from International Trade
* Management 1
* Strategic Human Resource Management
* Development Economics II: Microeconomic Aspects of Development
* Compliance - Management and Economics
* Economics of Automation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found Economics of automation to be very insightful! Even if the professor did not upload the problem set solutions (she showed you the solution in class, to which you had to take almost manic notes). But in general I found all courses very insightful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to move unexpectedly, which cost me an additional 5-10k.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Mostly things were as expected. Housing was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure. I participated in a volunteer club, but besides that I did not participate in much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found it very insightful to participate in a volunteer cub, especially if oyu wish to learn the language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the museums! most are free and very interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust. There was minor differences. I think if you go as a dane you will be fine, I think other cultures found it slightly more difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn German. But I will say, I was surprised by how open everyone was, and I dont think German is a prerequisite for making friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The germans can be very stuck in a rule rigid mindset, and are not necessarily very critical thinkers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness! I have never been invited to so many coffee meet ups. Im still in shock.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for housing in good time, dont rely on the university. Apply for scholarships. Apply for a lot of preapprovals and go to multiple lectures on arrival, and pick from there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask people for coffee. They are very helpful in general.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many new people and speaking fluent German!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding affordable housing (I failed).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
